title: Batching tail latency: hypothesis matrix and playbook (wip)
content:
Summary:
This is a working investigation into a persistent increase in p95/p99 request latency that started after the 2026-02-12 batching coordinator change (PR 732). Symptoms are long tail latency spikes (p99 up from ~220ms to ~1.6-2.0s) across multiple clusters, intermittent host memory surges, and periodic request stalls that line up with high KV-cache spill counts. This doc contains timeline, telemetry, hypothesis matrix, experiments run so far, and a short-run playbook for on-call response and mitigation.

Impact:
- Affected fleets: eu-west-1 and us-west-2 serving pools (multi-tenant).
- User visible: p95 increased ~2-3x, p99 increased ~7-9x for generation endpoints between 2026-02-12 04:00 UTC and ongoing.
- Percent of requests hitting stall windows: ~0.6-1.2% overall but responsible for most SLO breaches and customer alerts.

Observed symptoms (user-facing):
- Long stalls mid-generation where streaming tokens pause for 500ms-2s then resume.
- Some requests return earlier-than-expected errors (502/524) when stall exceeds client timeouts.

Timeline (concise):
- 2026-02-12 03:45 UTC: Rollout of batching coordinator refactor (PR 732).
- 2026-02-12 04:20 UTC: Increase in control-plane deployment failures for shard-resync; some hosts restarted.
- 2026-02-12 05:10 UTC: First customer alert for degraded latency.
- 2026-02-14 to 2026-02-20: Multiple partial rollbacks and config toggles; temporary improvement but regressions reappeared.
- 2026-02-28: Correlation found between KV-cache spill high-water events and tail-latency spikes.
- 2026-03-01: Reproduction harness created (see Repro steps).

How to reproduce (dev cluster):
1. Seed tenant with long, streaming generation workload (openai-chat style, 1-3k context, steady QPS 8-12).
2. Configure batching window to 18ms and enable the new coordinator mode (feature flag: batch-coordinator-v2).
3. Drive KV-cache pressure by setting cache.max_entries low for the test host (env override).
4. Observe p99 and heap profiles over 30-90 minutes; reproduce stalls where spill counters > 300/min.

Telemetry & logs to check (quick):
- metrics.serving.batch.window_ms, metrics.serving.batch.size_histogram (p50/p95), metrics.kv_cache.spill_count, metrics.kv_cache.eviction_count, jemalloc.active_bytes, host.heap_growth_rate, process.uptime_restarts
- Relevant logs: serving-runtime/batcher (INFO/DEBUG), kvcache/evictor (WARN), host-oom watcher events
- Traces: correlate span.batch.wait with span.kvcache.lookup and span.kvcache.spill. Use trace id from sample request.

Key observations so far:
- Spikes in kv_cache.spill_count consistently precede tail spikes by 400-1200ms.
- Hosts experiencing stalls show transient +200MB deltas in jemalloc.active_bytes coincident with spill bursts; fragmentation metrics increase.
- When coordinator reduces batch size via dynamic autoscale, stalls reduce but throughput drops.
- No deterministic deadlock found, but several threads show lock contention on kvcache read-write paths during spill windows.

Hypothesis matrix (ranked):
1) KV-cache spill path blocks critical IO path (high confidence): heavy spill causes synchronous disk/io operations or expensive marshaling on the request path, holding batch locks and delaying other requests. Evidence: timing correlation; evictor logs show synchronous flush logs during spikes.
2) Batching coordinator change increased lock hold time (medium-high confidence): new coordinator holds a global batching mutex for slightly longer during spill handling, amplifying tail. Evidence: perf stack traces show batch coordinator in top of block during stalls.
3) Memory fragmentation + jemalloc delay (medium confidence): repeated small allocations during spill cause fragmentation and temporary slowdown; observed active_bytes jumps.
4) Backpressure inversion between prefetch and eviction (low-medium): prefetch attempts to fill KV and triggers eviction cascade, creating oscillation. Evidence: some traces show prefetch > eviction loop overlap.
5) External dependency (disk, NFS) slower in affected AZs (low): less evidence; spill path is usually memory-backed but falls back to spill-to-disk in some configs.

Experiments executed and results (short):
- Experiment A: Disabled batch-coordinator-v2 on a canary fleet (2026-02-15). Result: latency dropped to baseline on canary but other fleets still exposed (partial rollback helps).
- Experiment B: Force async spill (convert sync spill to background worker) in test branch; ran on staging with synthetic load. Result: tail spikes reduced but observed memory bump in background workers; further tuning needed.
- Experiment C: Increased kv_cache.reservation threshold (fewer spills) on a tenant subset. Result: reduction in spill_count and tail-latency for affected tenants; suggests spills are causal.

Preliminary root cause (working):
Combined effect: the coordinator change exposed a hot path where synchronous KV-cache spill and additional lock hold time amplify batching contention. Under load, spill bursts transiently block request-handling threads and increase heap churn, producing the observed p99 spikes.

Short-term on-call playbook (tickets and mitigation):
1) If p99 > 800ms for >5 minutes and spill_count > 150/min, escalate to oncall-sre and serving-runtime owner.
2) Mitigate by toggling feature flag batch-coordinator-v2=false for the affected pool (hotfix rollback): use infra runbook to flip feature flag via rollout tool. Expected effect: immediate reduction in p99 but may drop throughput.
3) If immediate rollback not possible, tune kv_cache.max_entries / kv_cache.reservation upward for the pool to reduce spills.
4) As a fallback, scale the serving pool horizontally by 10-20% to reduce per-host pressure.
5) If host memory growth > 1GiB in 10m, cordon host and collect heap profile (pprof) before restart.

Commands and snippets (use with care):
- Toggle feature flag (infra CLI): infra flags set batch-coordinator-v2 false --selector cluster=eu-west-1 --namespace serving
- Increase kv cache threshold (hot override): kubectl -n serving set env deployment/serving-runtime --env="KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=200000"
- Collect jemalloc stats via proc endpoint: curl http://<host>:9090/debug/malloc-stats
- Generate heap pprof: curl -s http://<pod>:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-$(date +%s).pb
- Quick trace fetch: go run tools/tracefetch -id <trace-id> --service serving-runtime

Longer-term fixes (candidates):
- Make KV-cache spill fully asynchronous and bounded so it cannot block request paths; implement backpressure tokens rather than blocking locks.
- Rework coordinator to avoid global lock hold during spill handling; introduce per-batch lock or lock-free queue.
- Improve jemalloc tuning and reduce allocation churn during spill; consider slab allocation for spill buffers.
- Add stricter telemetry and alerting for kv_cache.spill_count and per-host jemalloc fragmentation percent.

Telemetry checks to add (short):
- Alert if kv_cache.spill_count > 100/min and p99 > 600ms in same 1m window.
- Add jemalloc fragmentation ratio gauge to per-host dashboard.
- Record batch lock hold time histogram and expose p99 for tracing.

Runbook draft for run-of-the-mill OOC triage (for on-call use):
1) Verify alert and collect sample trace ids and host ids.
2) Check spill_count and jemalloc.active_bytes on top offending hosts.
3) If spill_count confirmed high, and feature flag is on, rollback flag for affected selector.
4) If rollback not possible, increase kv_cache reservation and scale cluster.
5) After mitigation, keep monitoring for 30m; collect heap profiles if memory jumps continue.
6) Open follow-up ticket linking to SRV-1248 and assign to serving-runtime for full fix planning.

Open action items / next steps:
- [ ] Finish async-spill prototype and test under production-like load (owner: Ravi). ETA: 2026-03-18.
- [ ] Add batch lock hold-time telemetry and dashboard (owner: Liam). ETA: 2026-03-10.
- [ ] Schedule postmortem once full root cause confirmed; include stakeholders from platform-engineering and applied-ml.
- [ ] Update customer-facing incident notes and CS playbook if rollback will affect throughput.

Owners and contacts:
- Oncall SRE: rotation (use oncall tool)
- Primary investigator: Sofia Chen
- Serving runtime owner: Ravi Kumar
- Coordinator code owner: Liam O'Connor

Notes and open questions:
- Need to validate whether spill fallback-to-disk path was exercised in production by any host; if so, disk latency could be amplifying the effect.
- Confirm whether any tenant-level patterns (model size, sequence length) make certain tenants more sensitive.

Appendix: useful links and artifacts
- Jira: SRV-1248 (investigation & mitigation)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/732 (coordinator refactor)
- Staging experiment branch: feature/async-spill-proto
- Slack channel: #sre-serving-batching (use pinned summary)

(End of working notes — this doc will be iterated as we validate experiments and land follow-ups)
